channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Scientists Stand Corrected
item.description: Science should be able to correct itself — that is part of its strength. In nicotine policy, the problem comes when early claims are treated as settled truth long after the evidence has moved on. Corrections matter because public understanding of vaping, risk and smoking is shaped by what researchers, media and regulators choose to repeat. Public health should be willing to update its message when the data no longer supports the alarm. (Published on August 11, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: The high street you knew has gone forever
item.description: The changing high street tells a wider story about regulation, cost and unintended consequences. When legal businesses are squeezed while illicit trade expands, communities do not become healthier or safer — they lose accountable retailers and gain harder-to-control markets. Tobacco and nicotine policy should pay attention to that pattern. If regulation makes responsible shops disappear, the gap will not stay empty for long. (Published on August 11, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Finding Optimism in the Tobacco Harm Reduction Maelstrom
item.description: Optimism in tobacco harm reduction does not come from pretending the work is easy. It comes from the evidence that change is already possible: smoking can fall, safer alternatives can reach people, and public health can move beyond abstinence-only thinking. The setbacks are real, from prohibition to misinformation, but so are the lives improved when smokers find a route away from combustion. Harm reduction is ultimately a reason to keep going. (Published on August 11, 2026byfiltermag.org)
